description: Autonomous orchestrator recycle CORE: cycle-close arms a dedicated marker, a wrapper-owned watcher SIGTERMs the orchestrator claude, and the fresh respawn rehydrates via an explicit signal (CAM-141 fix), removing the manual /exit.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms hooks CANNOT terminate an interactive session: Stop/SubagentStop can only force continuation (exit 2 / continue:false), and no hook can initiate session termination. Sessions end via /exit, Ctrl-C, or an external signal (SIGTERM). Validates the CAM-162 decision that the wrapper (not a hook, not the sidecar) owns termination via SIGTERM on the PID.

Documents --session-id, --model, and --permission-mode (all already used by the orchestrator pane command). No in-session self-exit primitive is documented; interactive sessions are terminated externally, confirming SIGTERM-on-PID as the deterministic recycle mechanism.

userStories.title: Arm the recycle marker via cam journal append --cycle-close

acceptanceCriteria: `cam journal append --cycle-close` is a NEW flag: parseJournalArgs returns a `cycleClose` boolean on the append mode, distinct from `force`. [oracle: grep -q 'cycleClose' index.ts]

On the --cycle-close path, AFTER the durable writes (CAM_JOURNAL_APPENDED + the cycle-tokens event), dispatchJournal writes the recycle marker (.claude/.cam-orch-recycle, via the ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER constant) ONLY when the handoff file .claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json already exists. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts]

The discriminator for arming is the FLAG: `cam journal append --cycle-close --force` (cycle-close re-run after a failed push, journal entry already present + handoff present) still arms the marker. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts]

The non-flag path is byte-identical to today: a plain `cam journal append` never writes the recycle marker, and the two existing dispatchJournal tests at journal-append.test.ts:357 and :448 pass WITHOUT modification. [oracle: bun test test/commands/journal-append.test.ts]

userStories.title: Recycle watcher module and cam orch-recycle-watch command
userStories.description: As the wrapper, I need a watcher that detects the recycle marker, resolves the orchestrator claude PID without a new tmux surface, sends a graceful SIGTERM, and consumes the marker once, so termination is deterministic and does not re-fire on the respawn.
acceptanceCriteria: A new module src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts implements a poll loop that detects the recycle marker (ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER), and on presence resolves the orchestrator claude PID, sends SIGTERM, then removes the marker. [oracle: grep -rq 'ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER' src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts]

The watcher fires SIGTERM on the presence of the MARKER, never on the handoff file; a unit test with injected deps proves SIGTERM is sent when the marker is present and NOT sent when only a handoff (no marker) is present. [oracle: bun test test/commands/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]
The kill signal is a graceful SIGTERM (signal 15), not SIGKILL, so claude can exit cleanly; a unit test asserts the signal value. [oracle: bun test test/commands/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]

Consume-once: after firing SIGTERM the watcher removes the marker so a single arm triggers at most one SIGTERM (it does not re-kill the respawned session); a unit test asserts exactly one kill per marker arm. [oracle: bun test test/commands/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]

The PID is resolved WITHOUT opening a new tmux surface: the watcher reads the current orchestrator session-id fresh each poll from ORCH_SESSION_MARKER (.cam-orch-session) and scopes PID resolution to it (e.g. pgrep -f on the session-id). [oracle: grep -q 'ORCH_SESSION_MARKER' src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts]
The watcher does not call tmux (keeps the no-new-tmux-surface invariant). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

`cam orch-recycle-watch` is registered as an INTERNAL subcommand in index.ts (not listed in top-level HELP), invokable via Bun.spawn like `cam sidecar`. [oracle: grep -q "case 'orch-recycle-watch'" index.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
Full quality spine passes with no --no-verify (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: New file: src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts. Register in index.ts near the 'sidecar' case (~line 1554), mirror its INTERNAL-command comment. Make all I/O injectable (readMarkerFn, readSessionIdFn, resolvePidFn, killFn, sleepFn) so unit tests never touch real fs/processes -- follow the sidecar.ts dep-injection pattern. Read ORCH_SESSION_MARKER + ORCH_RECYCLE_MARKER from src/tmux/session.ts. PID resolution hint: the claude argv carries `--session-id <uuid>` (run.ts buildOrchestratorPaneCommand), so `pgrep -f <uuid>` scopes to this project's orchestrator with no tmux call; read the uuid fresh each poll (it is rewritten on every respawn, and is already lowercased in run.ts per the macOS uuidgen lesson). GOTCHA F-05: directory-grep oracles use grep -rq. Do NOT add token/occupancy logic here -- the occupancy backstop is CAM-163 (blocked by this issue); do NOT reuse parseTranscriptUsage/computeOrchBudget.

userStories.title: Wire the recycle watcher into cam run and prove SIGTERM+respawn end-to-end
userStories.description: As an operator, I need `cam run` to spawn the recycle watcher as a wrapper-owned co-process so that arming the marker terminates the orchestrator claude and the wrapper respawns it automatically, proven by an end-to-end integration test.
acceptanceCriteria: `cam run` spawns `cam orch-recycle-watch` as a background co-process when it creates a new session (mirroring the sidecar spawn), and kills it in the SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup handler alongside the sidecar. [oracle: grep -q 'orch-recycle-watch' src/commands/run.ts]

The recycle mechanism is proven end-to-end by an integration test (test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts) using a fake-claude under the real bash wrapper in a real tmux session: arming the recycle marker causes the fake-claude to receive SIGTERM and the wrapper to respawn a fresh fake-claude; the test skips gracefully when tmux is unavailable. [oracle: bun test test/integration/orch-recycle-watch.test.ts]
The termination mechanism is SIGTERM on the PID owned by the cam run wrapper: NOT send-keys, NOT a Claude Code hook, NOT the sidecar (the sidecar remains untouched). [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

AC13 ceremony (tracked, not dropped): the empirical validation that a REAL claude process exits cleanly on SIGTERM is captured as a follow-up issue filed via /cam-issue before ship. Per the CAM-162 spec the planner does NOT emit an operator story for this; the automated fake-claude integration test above covers the mechanism deterministically while this criterion tracks the real-claude ceremony obligation. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]

userStories.title: Explicit rehydrate delivery on respawn (CAM-141 fix) with cold-start safety
userStories.description: As a fresh orchestrator respawn, I need the wrapper to hand me the exact handoff path via an explicit signal so I rehydrate deterministically, and I must cold-boot cleanly when no such signal is present, so recycle no longer silently loses context every cycle.
acceptanceCriteria: On respawn, the wrapper exports CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE=<exact consumed handoff path> to the re-exec'd claude (buildOrchestratorPaneCommand, after the handoff is renamed to .consumed.json). [oracle: grep -q 'CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE' src/commands/run.ts]

The boot prompt (buildOrchestratorBootPrompt) instructs the fresh orchestrator to rehydrate ONLY when CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE is present, reading exactly that path; a unit test asserts the prompt string references CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE. [oracle: bun test test/run.test.ts]

Cold-start safe: when CAM_ORCH_REHYDRATE is absent the boot prompt directs a clean cold-boot and does NOT unconditionally read a stale .cam-orch-handoff.json / .cam-orch-handoff.consumed.json; the old unconditional 'if .cam-orch-handoff.json exists read it FIRST' instruction is removed. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

Consume-once + cap preserved: one handoff triggers at most one respawn (handoff renamed to .consumed.json before respawn) and DEFAULT_MAX_ORCH_RESPAWNS still bounds pathological write-then-exit loops; a unit test on the wrapper string asserts the rename and the cap are intact. [oracle: bun test test/run.test.ts]
